title: The mediating role of alexithymia in the relationship between family belonging and psychological resilience in English language teaching students
abstract: Abstract This study examined the associations among family belonging, alexithymia, and psychological resilience and the statistical mediating role of alexithymia among English Language Teaching (ELT) students. A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 177 ELT students and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). For the qualitative strand, 30 volunteers were randomly selected from the quantitative sample and interviewed using a semi-structured protocol; the data were analyzed through qualitative content analysis. The structural model demonstrated an overall acceptable fit ( χ² /df = 2.17, RMSEA = 0.082, SRMR = 0.055, CFI = 0.98, GFI = 0.94). Family belonging was positively associated with psychological resilience and negatively associated with alexithymia, while alexithymia was negatively associated with psychological resilience. The direct association between family belonging and psychological resilience was not statistically significant after alexithymia was included in the model ( β = −0.03, p > .05). A supplementary bootstrap analysis with 5,000 resamples showed a statistically significant indirect association through alexithymia ( b = 0.096, BootSE = 0.019, 95% CI [0.061, 0.136]). The qualitative findings complemented these results by contextualizing participants’ experiences of family belonging, emotional awareness and expression, and coping and recovery. Overall, the findings provide context-specific insight into the interrelationships among these constructs among ELT students and may be particularly relevant to university students in similar educational and cultural contexts. Given the cross-sectional design, the indirect association should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal or temporal mechanism.
